quotes.text: Stripe supports OUSD and USDC for stablecoin balances, although transfers on the Tempo network use USDC.e
Enter your email to request access.
Stripe automatically enables stablecoin payments when you activate
Eligible US businesses, subject to onboarding and restricted-business exclusions
For stablecoin payments, the refund returns to the customer’s original wallet as stablecoins.

old_evidence.text: Customers can pay with their preferred crypto wallet, token and payment network, while completed stablecoin payments settle in your Stripe balance in USD.
Link guarantees the funds, meaning no changes are required to your existing integration.
Eligible US businesses, subject to onboarding and restricted-business exclusions
Stripe confirms that the payment succeeded.

findings: The Link stablecoin flow remains stable. It offers eligible US businesses a one-time customer-present payment option in USD, from 1 to 10,000 USD, on Payment Links, Stripe Checkout and Elements. Customers must be in supported countries. Link says activated integrations automatically enable the method, guarantees the funds in scope, and documents completed payments settling in the merchant's Stripe USD balance (old raw lines 7-23, new raw lines 8-36).

New customer enters details under Crypto, continues to Stripe Crypto, selects and authorizes a wallet, confirms the details and confirms payment in the wallet before Stripe confirms success. New customers automatically sign up to Link. Returning customers select their saved wallet, receive prefilled details, then confirm payment before Stripe reports success. Testing uses a funded testnet wallet. Refunds return in stablecoins to the original wallet and disputes are unsupported (old raw lines 25-56, new raw lines 38-69).

Root index line 7 reaches Stripe index lines 238-239, 441-445, 736 and 760. Link concept lines 44-61 and 169-173 supplies the existing route. Keep the new form plus glossary dated and accessible on the Link source and qualify the reciprocal direct Crypto concept lines 8-28 and 38-55 where readers could confuse direct and Link payment scope.

Besides the new interest form and glossary content, changed explicit numbering and the contractions in disputes are presentational. See diff lines 26-64. The See Also links and named supported integrations continue unchanged.
substantive_changes: November newly documents an email-based request-access/interest path (old raw lines 8-14, new raw lines 11-27, diff lines 10-24). Treat it as an added documented action in the capture. The existing automatic enablement sentence is unchanged, and the form supplies no approval or mandatory onboarding claim.

November adds the OUSD/USDC balance and Tempo USDC.e transfer parenthetical (old raw lines 7-10 and new raw lines 8-11, diff lines 5-10). This is substantive context about separate balance/transfer uses, not evidence that the Link checkout token, network, merchant settlement currency, or supported payment flow changed.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain the May 8, 2026 capture date (old raw line 2), eligible-US-merchant and supported-customer-country distinction, Link activation and no-extra-integration wording under its conditions, the three surfaces and one-time on-session USD 1–10,000 range (old raw lines 7-23).

Preserve the May testnet, new and returning wallet flow, default signup, original-wallet stablecoin refund and no-dispute statements (old raw lines 25-56). No account or paid result is established by an example or a prose flow.
conflicts: Mapped source lines 13, 17 and 19, Link concept lines 52 and 173, and Stripe index line 445 should avoid implying universal wallet/token/network eligibility. Both captures say customers choose a preferred wallet, token and network for supported customers, while eligible US merchants face onboarding and restricted-business exclusions and the transaction must be one-time and on-session, USD-presented and USD 1–10,000 on three named surfaces (old raw lines 7-23 and new raw lines 8-36). Date and scope merchant geography separately from the customer's supported country. The November Link payment-methods overview lines 40-52 corroborates per-session filtering by customer location and business/transaction requirements. Neither Link stablecoin capture supplies a comprehensive wallet/token/network matrix.

Both captures say activating Link automatically enables this funding method on supported existing integrations (old raw lines 10-23, new raw lines 11 and 25-36). The November interest section at lines 13-23 separately asks for email to request access, with a preview-interest form. Preserve both statements, with no inference that every eligible merchant must reapply or that submitting the form grants access or removes onboarding restrictions. The captures do not explain which accounts encounter the form or how the form relates to auto-enablement. Give a reciprocal eligibility warning where source and concept currently say no integration changes.

November new raw line 9 adds a glossary parenthetical naming OUSD and USDC for stablecoin balances and USDC.e for transfers on Tempo. This is balance and transfer terminology. It does not list payment tokens or networks accepted by Link, or change the surrounding USD Stripe-balance settlement statement for completed Link payments. The separately dated November stablecoin payment overview at lines 19-37, 61-71 and 141-163 lists direct Crypto-specific token/network, non-US preview, local-currency settlement and Billing scope. Its direct token table labels USDC on Tempo. Keep that table and the glossary's USDC.e wording in their respective scopes rather than transferring either to Link. Qualify the reciprocal Link and Stablecoin Payments concepts so the direct product's Billing, geography and settlement characteristics cannot be read as Link support.

Mapped source lines 19-23 and 27-29 should show the state boundary. Customer authorization, wallet selection or confirmation, Link signup and prefilling do not prove success. Stripe reports success after wallet confirmation in both routes, and only completed payments are documented to settle USD in the merchant's Stripe balance. Link's funds guarantee has that product scope and provides no payout arrival or live execution proof. Refunds go as stablecoins to the original wallet and disputes are unsupported (old raw lines 8-10, 25-56 and new raw lines 9-11, 38-69). Testing uses a funded blockchain testnet wallet, not a live transfer.
unresolved_questions: The captures do not establish a universal Link wallet/token/network list, which accounts should submit the new interest form, access approval timing, exact merchant bank payout timing, or runtime behavior for any account or transaction.

answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/stablecoins documents Link as the payment surface for eligible US businesses with onboarding and restricted-business conditions, and for customers in supported countries. Payment Links, Stripe Checkout and Elements support one-time, on-session USD payments from 1 to 10,000 USD. The guide says Link activation automatically enables the funding method and the funds guarantee means an existing eligible integration needs no changes. It separately shows an email request-access form and supplies no approval or universal requirement for that form (new raw lines 8-36). Testing requires a wallet funded on a blockchain testnet. New shoppers enter details, continue to Stripe Crypto, choose a wallet, authorize Stripe interaction and confirm payment details and wallet payment. They automatically sign up to Link. Returning shoppers use a saved wallet with details prefilled and still confirm in their wallet. Stripe then confirms successful payment. Only completed payments are described as settling in USD in the merchant's Stripe balance. Refunds go in stablecoins to the original wallet, and disputes are unsupported (new raw lines 38-69). The May 8 capture documents the same core payment limits, flows and outcomes (old raw lines 7-27 and 29-56). source-stripe-stablecoins-on-link.md keeps those core facts but incorrectly says any stablecoin, wallet, token or network. The new OUSD, USDC and Tempo USDC.e glossary wording covers Stripe stablecoin balances or transfers, and provides no Link checkout support matrix (new raw lines 8-11).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/stablecoins the November capture adds an email-based access-interest form and a glossary note describing OUSD and USDC for stablecoin balances and USDC.e for Tempo transfers. Step numbering and the disputes contraction are presentation changes (old raw lines 7-16 and 29-56, new raw lines 8-29 and 42-69). The form does not establish an approval event or displace the unchanged Link activation language. Keep both dated and preserve the May 8 capture in source-stripe-stablecoins-on-link.md. Correct the universal wallet, token and network wording there and on the reciprocal Link concept and index routes. Link-specific eligibility is supported customer countries, eligible US merchants, onboarding and restrictions, USD 1–10,000, one-time on-session, and Payment Links, Checkout or Elements (old raw lines 7-23 and new raw lines 8-36). The November direct Crypto overview separately describes its own token/network table, local-currency settlement, private previews and Billing support. The direct overview and the OUSD/USDC/USDC.e glossary do not extend Link's supported assets, geographies, recurring capability or settlement scope. Use a testnet wallet with testnet funds for testing. Wallet selection or confirmation and Link enrollment are distinct from Stripe-confirmed success and USD settlement into the merchant's Stripe balance, which gives no bank payout time. The captures do not identify a new server API or SDK version for Link. Stablecoin refunds return to the original wallet and disputes remain unsupported (old raw lines 25-56 and new raw lines 38-69).
